recommendations.rationale: The adopted change (holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.01) has no candidate profile. The improvement feedback records status 'execution_incomplete': simulation.run completed (output artifact 54bd35343d20f1929c52fc5c28579c9517d10d50483ed98e9856d74bd090d839) while evaluation.run was rejected with 'BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: active phase / protected downstream capacity' (execution_id 'not_executed'), and the feedback result and receipt are null. No candidate reach, holding or computation measurement therefore exists to compare with the baseline (terminal error 0.007642608585867386 m; mean update 17.26331904856488 s; 35 deadline misses over 35 updates; holding-window speeds 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s). No further candidate or saved-state check is authorized in this phase, so the weight change stays advisory and unvalidated until a decision phase with evaluation capacity re-authorizes a complete execution.

Do not stack further weight changes on an unmeasured one. The accepted hypothesis (residual tip speed inside the settling window) is still only 'possible': it rests on six summarized rows with every sampled speed above the 0.02 m/s limit while the smallest position error is inside the 0.01 m limit, and the one-step projection explanation remains 'insufficient_evidence' because those comparisons are projected-versus-serial endpoints, not full state agreement. Address the specific grant gaps first: no candidate profile/evaluation capacity, no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution, full warm plans and iteration traces not retained, and no legal local-comparison state (no saved baseline update with effective horizon 0.01 s was identified; cataloged per-update effective horizons are 5, 7 and 10 control intervals at a 0.01 s control period). Any later measurement showing lower holding speed together with larger holding position error, or higher update wall time or deadline misses, should be treated as a trade-off or adverse result rather than a pass.

attribution.reason: Within the six sampled holding rows every tip speed (0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s) exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit, while the smallest sampled position error (0.007642608585867386 m) is inside the 0.01 m limit and the largest (0.05813810428573256 m) is not; the failing criterion therefore includes a speed criterion that fails even at the row with the smallest position error. The revision does not weaken this characterization, and it does not strengthen it either: the adopted change (holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.01) produced no candidate profile, because evaluation.run was rejected with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and the feedback status is 'execution_incomplete'. Only six summarized rows and no paired per-row table were displayed, so this remains a bounded, testable characterization rather than a dominant-cause claim.

Recorded co-occurrence: mean_update_s 17.26331904856488 s against a 0.01 s control period, 35 deadline misses over 35 updates, and per-update optimization_solve_s of about 15.0-15.67 s at several distinct updates. Cataloged effective_horizon values (10, 10, 10, 10, 7 and 5 control intervals at updates 7, 9, 10, 24, 28 and 30) show that at least these updates had short effective horizons while still recording long solve times. This documents that synchronous update computation exceeds the control period while every update is flagged as a deadline miss; synchronous wall overruns do not by themselves establish skipped simulated updates, and no causal link to the holding outcome is established.

The selected prediction batches compare a projected GVS endpoint against a full serial-backend endpoint, not full state agreement, and cover selected endpoint times rather than the whole trajectory; a projected-model probe cannot explain an entire settling outcome, and no paired per-row holding comparison against projections is displayed in this context.

Long optimization solve times of similar magnitude (~15.0-15.67 s) are recorded at several distinct updates rather than at one point, so the ~17.26 s mean update duration is not an artifact of a single anomalous update.

The adopted decision (control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.01) is recorded, but the associated complete execution is incomplete: simulation.run completed while evaluation.run was rejected with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED (execution_id 'not_executed') and the feedback result and receipt are null. With no candidate holding, reach or computation measurements, the effect of the weight change on holding speed, on holding position error and on update wall time is untested rather than supported or refuted; adoption alone executes nothing and a lower speed with a worse position would be a trade-off, not a pass.

facts.statement: Terminal instant (single sample, retained summary): tip position error is 0.007642608585867386 m - identical to the value cataloged for detail.late_motion[5].error_m - while the run summary reports sampled_settling_passed = false, holding_speed_passed = false and joint_reach_holding_passed = false. The same run reports reach-only success (reach_passed = true against the 0.01 m reach tolerance), so the official reach-only outcome and the joint reach-plus-holding outcome differ for this execution. Coverage: one terminal instant plus run-level flags, not the whole trajectory.

Final holding window (t = 0.30-0.35 s; all six recorded samples, row_count = 6): tip position error spans 0.007642608585867386-0.05813810428573256 m and tip speed spans 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s, against settling limits of 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s. Every one of the six sampled tip speeds exceeds the 0.02 m/s limit, while the smallest sampled position error lies inside the 0.01 m limit and the largest exceeds it; holding_speed_passed = false and sampled_settling_passed = false. Coverage: these six sampled rows only, not whole-trajectory ranges.

Holding-row structure: the summary preserves only a row count (6) and separate error and speed ranges, plus isolated per-row late-motion error leaves (0.007642608585867386 m for the last late row; 0.03407510504995951 m for late_motion[2]); cataloged late-motion sample times are 0.33 s and 0.34 s for rows 3 and 4. The terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s equals the reported minimum holding-window speed, so the row carrying the smallest sampled error also carries the smallest sampled speed. A paired per-row (error, speed) table was not displayed, so whether sampled holding error and sampled holding speed vary together or independently across the six rows is not determinable here; the equalities are numeric coincidences in reported values, not evidence of a causal link.

Computation (run summary plus per-update solve-time leaves): mean_update_s = 17.26331904856488 s against a 0.01 s control period, deadline_misses = 35 and update_count = 35, with configured max_iterations = 120. Cataloged per-update optimization_solve_s values are about 15.0-15.67 s at several distinct updates (15.002923699794337; 15.072048399830237 and 15.335863699903712; 15.37857409985736; 15.54932660004124; 15.67215109989047; 15.079233200056478), so the long solve times are not confined to one anomalous update. Coverage: run-level scalars plus the per-update leaves present in this catalog.

Per-update controller evidence present in this catalog: effective_horizon values of 10, 10, 10, 10, 7 and 5 control intervals at updates 7, 9, 10, 24, 28 and 30; optimization_raw_status 'User_Requested_Stop' at updates 7, 9, 11 and 30; policy_stop_reason 'budget_best_feasible' at updates 17 and 24 and 'relative_seed_improvement' at update 29; optimization_selected_iteration = 0 at updates 0, 3, 8, 11, 20 and 26. Coverage: a subset only - per-update horizon and solver/optimization status leaves for the remaining updates are not displayed in this catalog, and the run-level stopping counts appear only in the common summary, not as cataloged per-update leaves.

limitations: Coverage per area: terminal reach = single terminal instant plus run-level flags; sampled holding position and speed = the six recorded rows of the 0.30-0.35 s window only; computation = run-level scalars plus the per-update leaves present in this catalog (per-update effective_horizon and solver/optimization status only for a subset of updates).

Selected endpoints are not the full trajectory: prediction reads returned measured backend endpoints for controller updates 0-34 in batches of at most eight, and the motion view displayed only the six final-window rows; no continuous-time reconstruction or trajectory-wide paired table was displayed.

The improvement execution did not produce a candidate profile: status 'execution_incomplete', simulation output artifact 54bd35343d20f1929c52fc5c28579c9517d10d50483ed98e9856d74bd090d839 (no numbers displayed here), evaluation.run rejected with 'BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: active phase / protected downstream capacity' (execution_id 'not_executed'). No candidate-versus-baseline arithmetic is available, and campaign_comparison is null, so no candidate-minus-baseline difference is asserted.

Specific grant gaps: (a) no candidate profile / evaluation capacity, so the adopted weight change could not be measured; (b) no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution capability, and causal_identification is declared unsupported; (c) full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent); (d) the local-comparison grant was not exercised because no saved baseline update with effective horizon 0.01 s was identified - cataloged per-update effective horizons are 5, 7 and 10 control intervals at a 0.01 s control period; (e) the backend_motion raw record is a gzip octet-stream that cannot be read as JSON via evidence.read and must be accessed through the derived motion view.

Terminal-instant values are kept distinct from holding-window samples; the coincidence of the terminal error value with the minimum holding-window error (and of the terminal speed value with the minimum holding-window speed) is a numeric equality in reported values, not evidence of a causal link.

The fact catalog is a compact selection of scalar leaves; per-row values not listed are not asserted, and derived counts and ranges are quoted with their stated row coverage. No dominant cause is established.
recommended_actions: Advisory only: keep the accepted hypothesis (residual tip speed in the settling window) advisory and unvalidated; the adopted holding_tip_speed_weight change has no candidate measurement because evaluation.run was rejected with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, so a later decision phase should re-authorize a complete execution with evaluation capacity before any further tuning.

Advisory only: address the named coverage gaps before another decision - a paired per-row (error, speed) table across all 35 sampled backend timestamps, per-update effective_horizon and solver/optimization status for all 35 updates, and retained warm plans/iteration traces - and note that no legal local-comparison state (effective horizon 0.01 s) was identified among the cataloged updates.

Advisory only: treat any future candidate that lowers holding-window tip speed while raising holding position error, or that raises update wall time or deadline misses, as a trade-off/adverse result rather than a pass, and do not report a dominant cause from these bounded, partly-sampled records.
